identity.name: Kumari
identity.botanical_name: Aloe vera (L.) Burm.f. (syn. Aloe barbadensis Mill.)

classification.habit: Perennial succulent, stemless or short-stemmed herb with thick fleshy spiny-margined leaves in rosette
classification.habitat: Dry, sandy, well-drained soils in open sunny places; widely grown in gardens and fields.
classification.distribution: Cultivated throughout India and naturalised in drier regions, especially Rajasthan, Gujarat and the peninsular coasts.

identification.description: Sessile rosette succulent with thick fleshy lanceolate leaves, spiny margins and abundant translucent inner gel.
identification.whole_plant: Stemless or short-stemmed perennial succulent 30–60 cm high with a dense rosette of fleshy leaves and suckers at the base.
identification.stem: Very short, stout stem hidden by the leaf bases; spreads by basal suckers.
identification.leaf: Thick, fleshy, lanceolate leaves 30–50 cm long, grey-green, with spiny-toothed margins; inside is a colourless mucilaginous gel, and a yellow bitter juice lies just beneath the rind.
identification.flower: Tubular, pendulous yellow flowers in a dense raceme on a tall scape.
identification.fruit: Three-valved capsule; rarely formed under cultivation in India.
identification_points: Rosette of thick fleshy grey-green leaves
Yellow bitter juice beneath the rind
Yellow tubular flowers on a tall scape

therapeutics.precautions: Kanyasara (Elua, dried juice) is a strong purgative: prolonged use can cause loss of electrolytes such as potassium and may interact with digoxin and diuretics. The leaf gel is milder; topical use can occasionally cause contact dermatitis.
therapeutics.contraindications: Pregnancy (Artavajanana and purgative), lactation, intestinal obstruction, inflammatory bowel disease, abdominal pain of unknown cause, and young children (for Kanyasara).

shlokas:
कुमारी भेदनी शीता तिक्ता नेत्र्या रसायनी। मधुरा बृंहणी बल्या वृष्या वातविषप्रणुत्॥
गुल्मप्लीहयकृद्वृद्धिकफज्वरहरी हरेत्। ग्रन्थ्यग्निदग्धविस्फोटपित्तरक्तत्वगामयान्॥
nighantu_references: Bhavaprakasha Nighantu, Guduchyadi Varga; principal verse around 229–230 in searchable recensions
classical_reference.shloka_reference_status: corrected_2026-10-28; verify against printed Bhavaprakasha Nighantu
reference_hubs: TDU Indian Medicinal Plants Database — Shlokas

phytochemistry.chemical_notes: The purgative action of Kanyasara comes from anthraquinone glycosides such as aloin, while the inner leaf gel is mainly water and polysaccharides.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Known as Aloe Vera, Kumari is a premier herb for skin, liver detoxification, and regulating menstruation.
recognized_uses: Leaf gel applied to minor burns, wounds and skin irritation
Dried juice (Kanyasara) used as a purgative and emmenagogue
Ingredient of Kumaryasava and Rajahpravartini Vati
modern_information.safety_notes: Oral aloe latex products are stimulant laxatives and are not suitable for long-term use; gel used topically is generally well tolerated.

exam_points: Botanical name: Aloe vera (syn. Aloe barbadensis); Family: Asphodelaceae (Liliaceae)
Useful parts: leaf pulp/gel and Kanyasara (Elua, dried leaf juice)
Rasa: Tikta-Madhura; Guna: Guru-Snigdha-Picchila; Virya: Sheeta; Vipaka: Madhura
Key karma: Bhedana, Artavajanana, Rasayana, Yakrit-Plihahara
Active principle of Kanyasara: aloin (anthraquinone glycoside)
viva_questions: Why is Kumari avoided in pregnancy?
Name the active principle of aloe juice.
identification_points: Fleshy spiny-margined leaves in a rosette
Kanyasara: dark brown to black brittle masses with nauseous bitter taste
student.quick_revision: Kumari — Aloe vera (L.) Burm.f. (syn. Aloe barbadensis Mill.); Asphodelaceae (Liliaceae); part: leaf gel/pulp, dried resinous leaf juice (Elua); Rasa tikta, madhura; Guna guru, snigdha, picchila; sheeta virya; madhura vipaka.

teaching_points: Distinguish the leaf gel (soothing, Brimhana) from Kanyasara (purgative) as separate drugs.
Explain Kumari as an Artavajanana drug in Rajorodha and Kashtartava.
discussion_points: Safety of oral aloe latex versus topical gel.
Kumari as a Yakrit-Plihahara drug in Kumaryasava.
practical_points: Cut a fresh leaf to show rind, yellow juice and inner gel.
Examine a Kanyasara sample for colour, fracture and taste.

doctor.quick_reference: Kumari leaf pulp is Sheeta and Bhedana, used in Rajorodha, Yakrit-Pliharoga, Gulma and Vrana; Kanyasara 125–500 mg is a strong purgative to be avoided in pregnancy.
key_precautions: Kanyasara: not for long-term use (electrolyte loss)
Avoid in intestinal obstruction and IBD
